question: Ticket 1941e93b25a3 says 'No falsifier clause or design statement about committing the declared folder', but outline 5.3.5.2.3 reads "Declaring a new instance rotates, explicitly or implicitly: --new rotates explicitly, no flag rotates implicitly, --name overrides both. -amm Reading (superclaude is the rescue service's launcher, cairn/devices/cc/superclaude; none of these needs a folder prepared by hand): - `cairn superclaude --new` always rotates explicitly to the next undeclared n (cc_1 when cc_0 is declared, cc_2 when cc_1 is, and so on), then declares, wires and launches it. - `cairn superclaude` with no flag rotates implicitly: it starts cc_0 when cc_0 is free, and when cc_0 is taken (running) it rotates as --new does. - `cairn superclaude --name <x>` uses exactly x and overrides all of that: it declares x if absent, then launches it. - The declared folder commits through the door in the same act, so the house tree is not left dirty and crossings are not refused. - The one CC inference here: "implicitly" is read as taken (running) cc_0 means rotate, while a declared-but-stopped cc_0 is simply started. Tickets: aa05710a5124 reshapes to this; d13859e2ae46 is the implicit rotation; 0f7a8cada1ca names the next undeclared n. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator" (Outline requires 'The declared folder commits through the door in the same act, so the house tree is not left dirty and crossings are not refused.' The ticket's design omits any mention of committing the folder through the artifact door, suggesting this requirement may not be implemented.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Not this ticket. Instance declaration, rotation and the declared-folder commit are tickets aa05710a5124, d13859e2ae46 and 0f7a8cada1ca; this ticket ports the held-instance move only, and bounds.out now says so.
